title: The Payphone and the Constellation: a Hacker out of Palermo, and the Machine That Owns Itself

segments.name: Palermo, and the Machines Taken Apart

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the birth
stops.date_confidence: attested: 7 May 1975 on the Fundacion Konex biographical page and on Spanish Wikipedia. Some profiles give 1977; Infobae of 3 March 2018 calls him 43, which fits 1975. The Konex page does not state a birthplace, and the city rests on La Nacion's 2013 account of a Palermo childhood, so the pin is the Buenos Aires city centroid inherited byte-identical from cristina_fernandez_de_kirchner.journey.json and asserts no hospital.
stops.campa: A son is born on the seventh of May 1975 to Alfredo Kargieman and Ana Maria, both psychoanalysts, ten months before the generals take the country. He has a twin sister, Lucila, who will become a doctor in electroneurophysiology. The house runs on listening, on the slow reconstruction of what a person is made of out of what the person says. No hospital is recorded and no birth notice survives in anything reachable; the date enters the public record forty years later, in a Fundacion Konex biographical file that gives the day and the month and no birthplace at all.
suggested_refs: The Fundacion Konex biographical file b5038, the earliest checkable public record of the birth date

stops.name: Palermo, the house of the two psychoanalysts
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction for the date only. La Nacion 2013 and Infobae 2018 place the childhood in Palermo and record the dismantling of radios and other objects without dating any of it; 1980 orders the segment. The pin is the Palermo neighbourhood centroid, inherited byte-identical from javier_milei.journey.json, and marks no address.
stops.campa: The family lives in Palermo, and the boy takes the neighbourhood apart object by object: radios first, then anything held together by a screw. His parents' profession fills the house with talk about causes hidden under surfaces, and he goes at surfaces with a screwdriver. Nothing in the record says whether the radios went back together. By ten, Argentine press accounts have him repairing computers for other people, which is the first time the taking-apart earns anything. Of those years he keeps one sentence, given to an interviewer in 2026 when he was asked when it started.
stops.quote: Desde chiquito. No tengo recuerdo, pero si recuerdo los gritos de mis padres
stops.quote_source: EY / La Nacion, 'Hacedores que inspiran', episode 8, 21 August 2026. Diacritics restored in this transcription.
suggested_refs: The Palermo barrio of Buenos Aires, the ground of the childhood accounts
sources: La Nacion, 'Emiliano Kargieman: explorador del universo' (2013)

stops.name: Palermo, the Sinclair 2068
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. La Nacion 2013 names the machine as a Sinclair 2068 and says it arrived as he came to the threshold of adolescence, roughly age twelve or thirteen, so about 1987 or 1988; the widely repeated 'first computer at nine' has no support in that article, though the 2026 EY interview has him programming at nine and a half. 1988-01-01 orders the segment and asserts no month.
stops.campa: The computer arrives as he crosses into adolescence: a Sinclair 2068, an awkward American-market machine, and with it the discovery that a game he keeps losing is only a text somebody else wrote. He goes into the code and changes the terms. La Nacion will report that he preferred studying less in order to have the hours to shut himself in with the machine. He is not good at the games, and when a reporter asks him about it a quarter of a century later he gives the reason in one line.
stops.quote: Como no era bueno jugando, los hackeaba
stops.quote_source: La Nacion, 'Emiliano Kargieman: explorador del universo' (2013), on why he began altering the code of the games
suggested_refs: The Sinclair 2068, the Timex-built machine sold into the Southern Cone in the mid-eighties
sources: La Nacion, 'Emiliano Kargieman: explorador del universo' (2013)
EY / La Nacion, 'Hacedores que inspiran' (21 August 2026)

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the modem
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction, and tagged R in the report. La Nacion 2013 puts the modem at about twelve, which would be 1987, while the same article puts the Sinclair at the threshold of adolescence; the two cannot both be pinned exactly and the file orders them Sinclair then modem without claiming the interval. The pin is the Buenos Aires city centroid; the boards had no address.
stops.campa: A modem follows the computer and the telephone line becomes a door. The bulletin boards of Buenos Aires are a few hundred people trading files and argument down copper at the speed of a held breath, and the etiquette he learns there is older than he is: information wants to be free, and the way to prove you understand a system is to be somewhere inside it you were not invited. He is twelve or thirteen, and there is nobody in the house who can check what the machine is doing. The phone bills are his parents'.
stops.quote: Hay una filosofia atras del hacker... la informacion quiere ser libre
stops.quote_source: EY / La Nacion, 'Hacedores que inspiran' (21 August 2026), on the ethos of the bulletin-board years. Diacritics restored.
suggested_refs: The Buenos Aires BBS scene of the late 1980s, unarchived and known mainly through participant recollection
sources: La Nacion, 'Emiliano Kargieman: explorador del universo' (2013)
EY / La Nacion, 'Hacedores que inspiran' (21 August 2026)

stops.name: Buenos Aires, thrown out of the Cangallo
stops.date_confidence: attested by La Nacion 2013 for the expulsion, its cause, and the move to the Colegio Nicolas Avellaneda in the afternoon shift; no year is given for any of it and 1990 only orders the segment. Contradiction left standing: Artopoulos's academic history of Core says the founders came out of the ORT technical schools, which cannot be squared with Cangallo and then Avellaneda for Kargieman specifically. Neither school's address is documented for him, so the pin is the city centroid.
stops.campa: He is sent to the Cangallo Schule and thrown out of its secondary school for breaking into the rector's office and papering it, wall and desk and floor, in toilet paper. He finishes at the public Colegio Nicolas Avellaneda, in the afternoon shift, which suits him. The Colegio Nacional de Buenos Aires, the school that sets the hardest examinations in the country and returns the country's officials, was within reach of a boy who tested well, and he did not want it. He gives a reason with no ambition in it at all.
stops.quote: No queria que me rompiesen demasiado las bolas
stops.quote_source: La Nacion, 'Emiliano Kargieman: explorador del universo' (2013), on not attending the Colegio Nacional de Buenos Aires. Diacritics restored.
suggested_refs: The Cangallo Schule, the German-language school of Buenos Aires, and the Colegio Nicolas Avellaneda
sources: La Nacion, 'Emiliano Kargieman: explorador del universo' (2013)
Alejandro Artopoulos, 'El caso de Core Security Technologies', H-industri@

stops.name: San Jose and Avenida de Mayo, the bar
stops.date_confidence: attested by La Nacion 2013 for the meeting place, the entrance ritual and the group name; the article dates the scene only to the early nineties, and 1992 orders the segment. The coordinate is the San Jose and Avenida de Mayo intersection geocoded through Nominatim, correcting a research-pool value that fell some 490 metres west near Congreso.
stops.campa: The circle meets in a filthy bar at San Jose and Avenida de Mayo, three blocks from Congress, and calls itself Hacked by Owls. Among the boys at those tables is Matias Travizano, who will be beside him again thirty years later on a Patagonian power project. Its members are between fifteen and twenty and they meet in the flesh because the modems are slow and prestige is not transmissible over copper. The entrance requirement is not a password but a target: you arrive having taken something difficult, you say what it was, and the table decides.
stops.quote: Era todo muy elitista. Si no demostrabas que habias hackeado algo importante no te hablaban. Ni siquiera te dejaban sentarse en sus mesas.
stops.quote_source: Matias Travizano, quoted in La Nacion, 'Emiliano Kargieman: explorador del universo' (2013). Diacritics restored.
suggested_refs: The corner of San Jose and Avenida de Mayo, meeting ground of the early-nineties Buenos Aires hacker circle
sources: La Nacion, 'Emiliano Kargieman: explorador del universo' (2013)

stops.name: Centro Cultural Recoleta, the payphone
stops.date_confidence: attested by La Nacion 2013 for the conference, the hacked payphone and the text left on it; no day or month is given and 1994 orders the segment. The coordinate is the Centro Cultural Recoleta at Junin 1930 per Nominatim and the Wikipedia infobox, correcting a research-pool value about 170 metres south. The manifesto text is La Nacion's report of it, not an archival document.
stops.campa: A conference on hackers at the Centro Cultural Recoleta draws the press, and the press has decided that hackers are romantic. HBO, who take themselves for technicians rather than characters, open the building's public payphone and leave their answer running for whoever lifts the receiver next. It is not a manifesto in the American style, nothing about curiosity being a crime. It is a complaint about advertising: technology arrives with a label telling you what it is for, and the label is a lie.
stops.quote: Esta conferencia sucks... La tecnologia nos la venden con etiquetas que dicen para que usarla: todo eso es mentira.
stops.quote_source: The text left on the hacked payphone, as reported in La Nacion, 'Emiliano Kargieman: explorador del universo' (2013). Diacritics restored.
suggested_refs: The Centro Cultural Recoleta, Junin 1930, venue of the 1994 hacker conference
sources: La Nacion, 'Emiliano Kargieman: explorador del universo' (2013)

stops.name: Buenos Aires, Logical Backdoor in print
stops.date_confidence: attested that he appears at nineteen in Bonsembiante and Roberti's 1994 book under the handle Logical Backdoor, and that he broke off the interview; the report reaches this file through La Nacion 2013, since the book itself could not be obtained. Month is a placeholder.
stops.campa: Fernando Bonsembiante and Raquel Roberti collect the Buenos Aires scene into a book, Llaneros solitarios: hackers, la guerrilla informatica, and he is in it at nineteen under the handle Logical Backdoor. He breaks off the interview partway through because he has somewhere else to be. It is still the earliest printed record of that circle, and no later edition adds anything about him. Nineteen years afterwards a reporter asks him the question the book did not ask, whether the group ever wrecked what it entered.
stops.quote_source: La Nacion, 'Emiliano Kargieman: explorador del universo' (2013), answering directly whether HBO sabotaged the systems it entered
suggested_refs: Fernando Bonsembiante and Raquel Roberti, Llaneros solitarios: hackers, la guerrilla informatica (1994)
sources: La Nacion, 'Emiliano Kargieman: explorador del universo' (2013), citing Bonsembiante and Roberti (1994)

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the Grupo de Proyectos Especiales
stops.date_confidence: attested in Alejandro Artopoulos, 'El caso de Core Security Technologies' (H-industri@), which dates the recruitment chain to 1994 and names Cossio as the sponsor and Futoransky as the recruiter; La Nacion 2013 names only Cossio. The month is a placeholder. The agency is the DGI, which becomes AFIP only in 1997; no work address is documented, so the pin is the city centroid.
stops.campa: Ariel Futoransky takes a silver medal at the informatics olympiad in Stockholm, gives an interview to the Buenos Aires press, and is read by Ricardo Cossio, who runs the national tax bureau under Menem. Cossio offers him a post; Futoransky calls in Jonatan Altszul, Gerardo Richarte and Kargieman. Fifteen are hired, all under twenty, all olympiad medallists, into a Grupo de Proyectos Especiales with a double brief: catch the taxpayers billing off the books with software, and secure the bureau's own files against people exactly like themselves.
stops.quote: Obviamente era cuestionable, supongo, porque entrabamos en los sistemas de un banco, de una universidad o de una telefonica. Pero nunca hicimos dano, nunca robamos nada.
stops.quote_source: EY / La Nacion, 'Hacedores que inspiran' (21 August 2026), on what the group did before the tax bureau hired it. Diacritics as printed in the transcription reachable here.
suggested_refs: The Direccion General Impositiva before its 1997 reorganisation into AFIP
sources: Alejandro Artopoulos, 'El caso de Core Security Technologies', H-industri@

stops.name: Ciudad Universitaria, the mathematics abandoned
stops.date_confidence: attested that he studied mathematics at Exactas and did not finish; the enrolment year is not documented and the research pool's 1994 single-date anchor is unsupported, so 1995-03 orders the segment against the Argentine academic calendar. The pin is Pabellon II of Ciudad Universitaria, the Exactas building.
stops.campa: He enrols in mathematics at the Faculty of Exact and Natural Sciences, out at Ciudad Universitaria on the river, in the pavilion where the physics and the chemistry are done. He does not finish. The company he is about to start is already eating the timetable, and a degree in mathematics is a slow instrument for a man being paid to break things by Thursday. The enrolment year is documented nowhere; only the leaving is. He will come back to this building eighteen years later, to lecture in its Aula Magna.
suggested_refs: Pabellon II, Facultad de Ciencias Exactas y Naturales, Ciudad Universitaria
sources: UBA Exactas, 'Al abordaje de la carrera espacial' (29 May 2013)
La Nacion, 'Emiliano Kargieman: explorador del universo' (2013)

stops.name: Puan, the philosophy abandoned
stops.date_confidence: attested by La Nacion 2013, which describes a sequence and not two simultaneous accounts: he had already dropped mathematics and was enrolled in philosophy, which he would not finish either, and the same article names the corridors of Puan. The year is not given; 1996-03 orders the segment. Philosophy at the UBA is taught at Filosofia y Letras on Puan, not at Exactas, which corrects the research pool.
stops.campa: From Exactas he crosses the city to Puan 480 and enrols in philosophy, which he does not finish either. The corridors of Puan are, in the mid-nineties, the loudest place in Argentine intellectual life and the least employable. Thirty years on he will publish a paper arguing that companies operated by machines need a legal form, and he will build the argument out of Elinor Ostrom and Carl Schmitt, who are read in those corridors. He is twenty one, and Core is a few months old. What he carries out of Puan is not a degree.
suggested_refs: Facultad de Filosofia y Letras, Puan 480, Buenos Aires
sources: La Nacion, 'Emiliano Kargieman: explorador del universo' (2013)

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the AFIP myth
stops.date_confidence: the DGI's reorganisation into AFIP in 1997 is attested and fixes the anachronism; the date is an ordering device for a myth with no date of its own. The myth itself is [R]: a recurring formulation across later profile writing, contrasted against La Nacion 2013 and Artopoulos, neither of which contains a caught teenager.
stops.campa: The tax bureau becomes AFIP in 1997, and over the following decades the story of his recruitment migrates. The teenager is caught; the agency he broke into hires him; the state buys off its own burglar. Nothing in the record supports it. He was recruited through an olympiad medal and a newspaper interview, into an agency that did not yet carry the name the myth gives it, to test systems nobody says he had entered. He has never worked very hard at the correction.
stops.quote: si lo hubiesemos hecho jamas te lo contaria
stops.quote_source: La Nacion, 'Emiliano Kargieman: explorador del universo' (2013), the immediate follow-up to his denial that the group sabotaged anything. Diacritics restored.
suggested_refs: The 1997 merger of the DGI and the customs service into the Administracion Federal de Ingresos Publicos
sources: La Nacion, 'Emiliano Kargieman: explorador del universo' (2013)

segments.name: Core, the Company That Was a Kind of MBA

stops.name: Buenos Aires, six founders and a flat
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year and the six names in the H-industri@ history of Core Security, cross-read against La Nacion 2013. Contradiction left standing: the Fundacion Konex biography has him founding the company at nineteen, which would be 1994 or 1995. The flat in central Buenos Aires is reported without an address, so the pin is the city centroid. Month is a placeholder.
stops.campa: Six of them start the company: Ivan Arce, Ariel Futoransky, Gerardo Richarte, Jonatan Altszul, Lucio Torre and Kargieman, with the first office in Arce's flat in the middle of Buenos Aires. What they sell is the skill the tax bureau had already paid them for: knowing exactly how a system fails. He is twenty or twenty one, or nineteen if you take the Konex biography, which the founders' own accounts do not. In the retellings the six will narrow to four and then to two, as one face becomes the public one.
stops.quote_source: His own formulation for what the company was, reported by Forbes Argentina and El Cronista. The widely circulated 'Core fue mi MBA' is not verbatim and does not appear in La Nacion's 2013 profile.
suggested_refs: Alejandro Artopoulos, 'El caso de Core Security Technologies', the academic history of the company
sources: Alejandro Artopoulos, 'El caso de Core Security Technologies', H-industri@

stops.name: Buenos Aires, CoreLabs on Bugtraq
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction for the date. The advisory archive at coresecurity.com establishes CoreLabs and its Bugtraq publishing; the laboratory is placed about a year after the founding, which the sources support only loosely. Month is a placeholder.
stops.campa: About a year in, the company builds itself a laboratory whose product is not software but standing. CoreLabs publishes what it finds on Bugtraq, the mailing list where the world's system administrators read their bad news each morning, and every advisory signed out of Buenos Aires is an argument that serious security research happens in Argentina. From here there is no other way to be believed. The advisories go out free. The consulting contracts follow them north.
suggested_refs: The CoreLabs advisory archive at coresecurity.com
sources: coresecurity.com, Core Labs advisories
Alejandro Artopoulos, 'El caso de Core Security Technologies', H-industri@

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the SSH1 insertion attack
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day: CORE-SDI-04, posted to Bugtraq 11 June 1998, authors Ariel Futoransky and Emiliano Kargieman, archived at seclists.org.
stops.campa: On the eleventh of June 1998 Futoransky and Kargieman post CORE-SDI-04 to Bugtraq. An attacker able to alter traffic on an SSH1 session can splice in encrypted blocks that decrypt, on the far side, into commands the server will run. The protocol everyone had moved to in order to stop being watched turns out to be writable. It is read that week in every operating-system shop on earth. Both authors sign from an office in Buenos Aires, and the text of the advisory is still on the Bugtraq archive.
suggested_refs: CORE-SDI-04, the SSH1 insertion attack advisory, Bugtraq, 11 June 1998
sources: seclists.org, Bugtraq archive, June 1998, CORE-SDI-04

stops.name: Buenos Aires, Endeavor and the Canadian contract
stops.date_confidence: attested in Artopoulos: at the end of 1999 Endeavor named Core the entrepreneurial company of the year and Jonatan Altszul, not Kargieman, entrepreneur of the year. This corrects a research-pool claim dating both an Endeavor selection and a first United States penetration test to 1998; no source was found for such a test. The 1997 Ballista contract with Secure Networks and its 1998 purchase by Network Associates are attested in the same history.
stops.campa: At the end of 1999 Endeavor names Core the entrepreneurial company of the year, and names Jonatan Altszul, not Kargieman, its entrepreneur of the year. The company's first real foreign money had come two years earlier from Secure Networks, in Canada, for the Ballista scanner; when Network Associates bought Secure Networks in 1998, the American market opened by inheritance rather than by conquest. The tidier story, in which Core arrives in the United States on the strength of one penetration test, has nothing behind it.
suggested_refs: Endeavor Argentina's 1999 selections; the Ballista scanner contract with Secure Networks Inc.
sources: Alejandro Artopoulos, 'El caso de Core Security Technologies', H-industri@

stops.name: Sao Paulo, eight months and no beachhead
stops.date_confidence: attested in Artopoulos, who names the Brazilian office of 2000, Kargieman's eight-month move to run it, the failure to sell Core Force to the Brazilian arm of the Banco de Boston, and the fact that Core had no United States office at the time, operating instead from Altszul's New York flat. This corrects a research-pool claim of a first American office in New York in 2000. Month is a placeholder and no Sao Paulo address is documented, so the pin is the city centre.
stops.campa: He moves to Sao Paulo for eight months to open the company's first foreign office, looking for partners, salesmen, support engineers. It does not work. The Brazilian arm of the Banco de Boston will not buy Core Force, and the office that was to be the beachhead of a continental expansion closes without becoming one. Altszul is meanwhile working New York out of his own apartment, because there is no New York office either. The academic history of Core is the only place any of the eight months is written down.
suggested_refs: Core Force, the product the Brazilian expansion was built to sell
sources: Alejandro Artopoulos, 'El caso de Core Security Technologies', H-industri@

stops.name: Buenos Aires, CORE IMPACT
stops.date_confidence: attested that Ivan Arce presented on automating penetration tests in 2001 and that Core commercialised CORE IMPACT, which the company describes as the first commercial off-the-shelf automated penetration-testing product. The 2002 date and its month are placeholders for the commercialisation, which no reachable source fixes precisely. The attribution question is stated in the campa rather than resolved.
stops.campa: Ivan Arce gives a talk in 2001 on automating the penetration test, and the company turns it into a product: software that attacks a client's own network the way an attacker would, on a schedule, wearing a suit. Core calls it the first of its kind sold off the shelf. Profile after profile credits Kargieman with developing it; the surviving engineering record credits CoreLabs, collectively, and puts him in the laboratory as one name among several. Neither account has ever been corrected against the other.
suggested_refs: Ivan Arce, 'Automating Penetration Tests', 2001 presentation, coresecurity.com publications
sources: coresecurity.com, Core Labs publications
Alejandro Artopoulos, 'El caso de Core Security Technologies', H-industri@

stops.name: Boston, the headquarters in English
stops.date_confidence: attested in the H-industri@ history for the year of the move of the United States headquarters to Boston, with research and engineering remaining in Buenos Aires. No street address is reachable, so the pin is the Boston city centre. Month is a placeholder.
stops.campa: The American headquarters moves to Boston while the research and the engineering stay in Buenos Aires, an arrangement the company keeps for the rest of its independent life: the invoices in English, the work in Spanish. He crosses as one of five remaining partners and comes back to an office at home that now occupies floors. No street address for the Boston office survives in any reachable source, and nothing records how much of the year he spends in either city. He is twenty eight.
suggested_refs: The split-site model of Core Security: Boston sales, Buenos Aires engineering
sources: Alejandro Artopoulos, 'El caso de Core Security Technologies', H-industri@

stops.name: Buenos Aires, foundations for secure triggers
stops.date_confidence: attested: IACR ePrint 2005/284, revised in ACM Transactions on Information and System Security 9:1 (February 2006), authors Futoransky, Kargieman, Sarraute and Waissbein. The same ePrint version associates him with an ITBA doctorate in informatics engineering, which is an enrolment and not a completed degree. Month is a placeholder.
stops.campa: With Futoransky, Carlos Sarraute and Ariel Waissbein he publishes on secure triggers: cryptographic constructions that keep protected information invisible until a hidden condition is satisfied, and then release it. The paper goes to the IACR preprint server and on into ACM Transactions on Information and System Security. One version of it lists him as a doctoral student in informatics engineering at ITBA. He does not finish that one either. Mathematics, philosophy, the doctorate: three enrolments left behind, and no source explains any of them.
suggested_refs: Futoransky, Kargieman, Sarraute and Waissbein, 'Foundations and Applications for Secure Triggers', IACR ePrint 2005/284
sources: IACR ePrint 2005/284
ACM Transactions on Information and System Security, vol. 9 no. 1 (February 2006)

stops.name: Buenos Aires, leaving at thirty
stops.date_confidence: attested that he left day-to-day involvement at about thirty, which places it in 2005; no source gives a month and June is a placeholder. Forbes Argentina and El Cronista carry the same account of the age at founding and at departure.
stops.campa: He leaves at about thirty. The company has four hundred and some people, an American headquarters, a product line, and eleven years of his life in it. He calls it, afterwards, a kind of MBA, and the phrase gets shortened in circulation until it reads as a dismissal, which it is not; he means that the thing was an education somebody paid him to receive, in law, in payroll, in how a system fails when it is made of people. What he does not say in any interview reachable here is why he went when he did.
stops.quote: Yo arranque la empresa con 18, 19 anos. Me fui cuando tenia 30. Los cinco socios que empezamos Core eramos unas 400 y pico de personas cuando yo me fui.
stops.quote_source: EY / La Nacion, 'Hacedores que inspiran' (21 August 2026). Transcribed as printed in the reachable text, diacritics stripped there; the sentence about the five partners is what makes the 400 figure a headcount.
suggested_refs: Forbes Argentina and El Cronista profiles carrying his own account of the Core years
sources: La Nacion, 'Emiliano Kargieman: explorador del universo' (2013)
EY / La Nacion, 'Hacedores que inspiran' (21 August 2026)

segments.name: The Wrong Side of the Table

stops.name: Buenos Aires, Aconcagua Ventures
stops.date_confidence: attested that he founded the fund with Gerardo Richarte and that he later described the venture-capital period as a mistake of his own; the founding year comes through his 2008 ITBA talk and the profile literature, with no month and no registered address reachable. Month and pin are placeholders.
stops.campa: With Gerardo Richarte he starts Aconcagua Ventures, an early-stage fund for Latin American technology companies, and works out within a couple of years that he has crossed to the wrong side of the table. No portfolio list survives and no registered address is reachable. Listening to other people's projects, giving advice, signing cheques: none of it is the work, and he calls the venture-capital passage a mistake of his own making, entered too young. Asked why, he answers on the level of appetite.
stops.quote: A mi lo que me gusta es hacer. Escuchar proyectos y dar consejos me empezo a aburrir
stops.quote_source: La Nacion, 'Emiliano Kargieman: explorador del universo' (2013), on leaving the fund. Diacritics restored.
suggested_refs: Aconcagua Ventures, the early-stage fund founded with Gerardo Richarte
sources: ITBA / South American Business Forum, 'Encuentros con Emprendedores Exitosos' (9 April 2008)
La Nacion, 'Emiliano Kargieman: explorador del universo' (2013)

stops.name: ITBA, telling the students how it happened
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by the South American Business Forum blog. The pin is the ITBA campus on Avenida Eduardo Madero; the room is not recorded.
stops.campa: He is invited to the South American Business Forum at ITBA to tell students how Core happened, and by 2008 the story has a shape: the boy with the modem, the tax bureau, six friends and a flat, four hundred employees. He is thirty three and has already had one whole career. The date is the ninth of April, and the room is not recorded. The students ask how a technology business gets built in Argentina. What he answered is not preserved in his own words anywhere, and neither is what he meant to build next.

stops.name: Moffett Field, ten weeks on a federal airfield
stops.date_confidence: attested that he attended the ten-week Singularity University Graduate Studies Program at NASA Research Park, Moffett Field, in 2010, and that he concluded satellites were built from outdated components. No month is documented; June orders the summer program. The pin is inherited byte-identical from ray_kurzweil.journey.json. He was never a NASA employee.
stops.campa: He spends ten weeks at Singularity University, the unaccredited program Ray Kurzweil and Peter Diamandis run out of leased buildings on a federal airfield at Moffett Field. He is not employed by NASA and has never been, whatever the profile writing keeps saying. He arrives curious about biotechnology and leaves looking at satellites. What he has seen is an industry assembling spacecraft from components a decade behind the telephone in his pocket, at prices set by the assumption that nothing can ever be tested twice and every launch must work.
